system.description: This is a golden, egg-shaped item roughly the size of a human’s fist.
system.unidentifiedDescription:
This is a golden, egg-shaped item roughly the size of a human’s fist. It is sentient, and will offer to ally with someone who treats it with respect and friendship. Whether or not the pod will accept your treatment is at the Narrator’s discretion. Once you have formed an alliance with the pod, it will make an offer of its gifts. If you accept the offer, you are able to attune to it.

A gilded pod is a sentient magic item, whose goal is to slowly convince its bearer to accept hindrances in exchange for increasingly powerful gifts. In a process not even understood by the pod, imposing these hindrances on its bearer somehow empowers it to provide the benefits.

Sentience. The pod is a sentient construct with Intelligence 14, Wisdom 10, and Charisma 18. It has hearing and darkvision to a range of 120 feet. The pod communicates with its bearer telepathically and can speak and understand Common, and any other languages frequently spoken in the region where it was found.

Personality. The gilded pod has no name of its own, and will answer to whatever identifier its bearer chooses. The pod’s purpose is to provide benefits in exchange for hindrances, happy with whatever its new ally decides. These are package deals, each week the offer is to accept a specific set of new benefits coupled with a matching hindrance, or don’t. Due to the strange nature of the pod’s hindrances powering its own benefits for each deal, it doesn’t need to push its bearer. If the gifts are not accepted for one week, it will happily wait for the next week, when a new set of powers and hindrances is up for discussion. The pod is subservient to its bearer, but its knowledge is limited to detailing its own abilities and hindrances. For example, when its bearer gains Plant Knowledge, it’s the bear who has the knowledge, not the pod.

Attunement and Identify

During the course of either attunement or use of the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.dgms08g84zdlbr81]{Identify} spell, the gilded pod makes itself known to the potential bearer, speaking telepathically and offering the following giftsgifta in exchange for the matching “downside”:

  • Benefit - Plant Knowledge: When you would normally make a check to recall knowledge about any plants or plant monsters, at the Narrator’s discretion you automatically have all desired knowledge. This knowledge also opens additional opportunities for finding rare plants. You gain one of the following:

    • You gain the druid Secret of Nature (knack), Gather Obscure Medicinals. You don’t need to meet the prerequisite, and this does not count against your number of knacks known.

    • Alternatively, you instead gain the druid Secret of Nature (knack) Herbal Apothecary, and this does not count against your number of knacks known.

  • Benefit - Psychic Resistance: You have resistance to psychic damage.

Hindrance - Detachment: Your demeanor will become detached, and this will be noticeable to your companions.

Week 2

At the beginning of the second week, the gilded pod again telepathically whispers to its bearer, offering another gift with another downside.

  • Benefit - Sleep: Once daily, you can cast the @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.qwng28nro7eme3nh]{Sleep} spell, but with a 2 hour duration. For determining hit points worth of creatures affected, the spell is treated as if using a spell slot equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down).

  • Benefit - Less Emotion: You gain an expertise die on all checks and saving throws to resist rage-inducing or fear-inducing effects, and the frightened condition. You are immune to all other emotion-manipulating effects, such as @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.ohrkuqnbaeutcwox]{Vicious Mockery}, @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.hnvt4tnuww6o4vvi]{Calm Emotions}, @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.t7b2d38omjqhli99]{Faux Pas}, or the lingering despair effect of @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.4tn3jxhf3pqv5o1l]{Despairing Hideous Laughter}.

Hindrance - Minor Fatigue. You will gain 1 level of fatigue at the end of each long rest. This can be removed as normal.

Week 3

At the beginning of the third week, the gilded pod whispers again, with more powerful gifts that come with a “minor” downside.

  • Benefit - Wallflower: At the beginning of each long rest, you can summon a @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-monsters.Actor.hwzfygsaqxtb9qkd]{wallflower}. It bursts from the earth at a location of your choosing, which could be a pot or other container. The plant will protect you as you sleep, and can be instructed to ignore up to 5 creatures of your choosing. You can only have one summoned wallflower at a time, and it will wither and die if you move more than 50 feet from it.

  • Benefit - Compassionless Inspiration. You now show a lack of compassion, concern, and care, choosing the best for yourself without regard for others. You gain inspiration any time you make a tactical move that protects yourself, while directly putting the safety of a companion at risk. Examples include allowing an ally to come to harm through action or inaction (as collateral damage, not as direct attacks), or intentionally putting companions in direct danger to gain an advantage in encounters. Note that from your perspective this is not evil, it is indifference.

Hindrance - More Fatigue. You will gain 2 levels of fatigue at the end of each long rest. Only 1 level can be removed through non-magical means.

Week 4

More gifts are offered at the beginning of the fourth week, but this time the downside might give the bearer pause.

  • Benefit - Spellcasting: While holding the gilded pod, you can expend charges to cast the following spells (+7 spell attack bonus, spell save DC 15):

    • @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.yhdfb6yywes7eswj]{Barkskin} (2 charges), @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.3fqncxt9imp9n4zc]{Locate Animals or Plants} (2 charges), @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.kgm6hw1eesrtcm29]{Insightful Speak with Plants} (3 charges), @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.fnuefdnb228qwwu8]{Plant Growth} – rapid option only (3 charges), @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.k213xxhuazt5uocn]{Awaken} (5 charges), @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.m68wvspmjjd2aaat]{Wall of Thorns} (6 charges)

    • The gilded pod has 10 charges and regains 1d6+4 expended charges each dawn.

  • Benefit - Plant. You gain the plant creature type, in addition to any prior creature types.

Hindrance - Even More Fatigue. You still gain 2 levels of fatigue at the end of each long rest, but now neither can be removed through non-magical means.

Week 5

The bearer now reaches the pinnacle of abilities available through the gilded pod.

  • Benefit - Extra Sleep: You can now cast your variant @UUID[Compendium.a5e.a5e-spells.Item.qwng28nro7eme3nh]{Sleep} spell twice daily, and it is now treated as if using a spell slot equal to your proficiency bonus.

  • Benefit - Hive Knowledge. You are able to access more of the hive mind. You gain an expertise die on checks made to learn legends and lore about a creature you can see, advantage if the creature is a plant or fungus.

  • Benefit - Gilded Touch. As an action, you can target a single creature within 15 feet to briefly connect its mind with the gilded pod. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against a DC of 10 + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (you choose) or become frightened of you and your allies for 1 minute. Creatures can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of their turns.

Hindrance - Sleep, Friend. Whenever you cast your sleep spell, one companion is also impacted. The companion gets no saving throw, but you can choose who is impacted.
